subject.title: feat(sandbox): add sbx as a sandbox backend alongside OpenShell

question: Should OpenClaw officially ship and document an `sbx` sandbox plugin that starts Docker Sandboxes, executes its CLI, and bind-mounts OpenClaw workspaces into the sandbox runtime?
rationale: This is an intentional product and security-boundary choice, not a mechanical defect: the code can follow the existing plugin seam while official support still commits the project to Docker Sandboxes’ daemon, policy, mount, authentication, and upstream CLI contract.

options.title: Sponsor after secops approval
options.body: Approve the official plugin only after sandbox owners and secops accept the executable, daemon, direct-mount, and dependency-graph boundaries for the reviewed head.

options.title: Keep it external
options.body: Decline official catalog and documentation support while leaving contributors free to distribute an independently maintained plugin through the normal plugin ecosystem.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after secops approval
recommendation.body: Approve the official plugin only after sandbox owners and secops accept the executable, daemon, direct-mount, and dependency-graph boundaries for the reviewed head.

likelyOwner.reason: No concrete current-main ownership trail was obtainable in the read-only environment; the decision belongs with the sandbox/plugin SDK and security owners.
